name: Apple Silicon Mac, 8 GB unified (M1-M3 base MacBook Air / Mac mini)
notes: The smallest Mac most people still carry. macOS lets the GPU use about 5.3 GB of the 8 GB by default (Metal working set 5,461 MiB on an 8 GB M1), so a 4-bit 4B model fits and a 9B does not.
Close other apps first: the browser and the model share the same 8 GB.
Apple stopped selling 8 GB Macs with the M4 generation (16 GB became the base), so this tier is M1-M3.

identity.name: Apple Silicon Mac, 8 GB unified (M1-M3 base MacBook Air / Mac mini)

memory.note: usable_gb is macOS's default Metal GPU budget (recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize), about two thirds of 8 GB on Macs this size; bandwidth is a per-chip property, so each variant carries its own

compute.cpu_cores: Apple Silicon; core counts vary by chip and SKU tier
compute.note: Apple publishes no GPU FLOPS for M-series chips. MLX and llama.cpp/Metal drive the GPU; the Neural Engine is largely unused by local-LLM runtimes.

thermal.cooling: fanless (MacBook Air) or active fan (MacBook Pro, Mac mini, iMac)
thermal.note: fanless Airs throttle under long generations; short chats are unaffected

variants.name: M1 8 GB
variants.note: Apple states M2's 100GB/s is 50 percent more than M1

sources.note: M2: 100GB/s unified memory bandwidth, 50 percent more than M1; up to 24GB
M4: 16/24/32GB options, 120GB/s; M4 Pro 24GB entry config, 273GB/s
M5: 153GB/s unified memory bandwidth, more than 2x over M1
Metal's recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize is the GPU budget llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio and MLX plan around; a 24 GB M3 log shows 16,383 MiB for the GPU at the default setting
real 8 GB M1 Mac mini reads a 5,461 MiB Metal working set
16 GB Apple M1 llama.cpp log: recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize = 10922,67 MiB
